newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran to recall EU envoys, IRNA says.
newsitem.headline: Iran to recall EU envoys, IRNA says.

text.p: Iran will recall its ambassadors from European Union states who have summoned their Tehran envoys after a German court's verdict that the Islamic republic ordered political killings in Berlin, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.
IRNA late on Saturday quoted a Foreign Ministry source as saying Iran would "reciprocate the decision of the (EU) governments to recall their ambassadors from Tehran".

EU members, with the exception of Greece, recalled their envoys for consultations following Thursday's Berlin court ruling that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Germany.
Iran, which has repeatedly denied all involvement in the killings, has urged EU states not to jeopardise their interests in Iran over the verdict.

Germany, until recently Iran's largest trading partner and most important Western friend, ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country and recalled its ambassador in Tehran immediately after the court verdict. Iran also recalled its ambassador and expelled four German diplomats.

Hundreds of slogan-chanting Iranians pelted the German embassy in Tehran with tomatoes on Friday and state-run Tehran radio said on Saturday that another protest march on the embassy was scheduled for Sunday.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Friday criticised the verdict but said the diplomatic row was a "passing storm" provoked by the United States and Israel.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Saturday that Iran must show respect for international law before Bonn could discuss a fresh start in relations.

Kinkel told the weekly Welt am Sonntag that Germany had no desire to end over a century of ties with Tehran despite the expulsion of the four Iranian diplomats and, jointly with its EU partners, ending a policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran.
"Iran must voice its commitment to international law and act accordingly. Then both sides must think about a fresh start," he said in an interview released ahead of publication on Sunday.
